key_insights: NDX closed Friday on its lows, back below its 50/100-day moving averages and through trend-line support, down about 550 bps on the week. It was the NDX's largest weekly decline since Liberation Day, led by Semis down about 11.5% on the week.

Franchise flows showed selling pressure across Tech and AI as the market re-priced growth expectations lower. The desk attributes this to rates and oil tensions and to a growing debate on whether the AI build-out is linear. GIR estimates AI capex contributes about half of S&P 500 EPS growth.
Few 'innings' style inbounds last week. Most client conversation was about testing thematic and fundamental convictions after several tough months, with a compressed calendar into year-end.

Unlike the July momentum unwind, which the desk calls largely technical after the April-June run, the current episode has investors debating which overhang is most acute or solvable into year-end. Candidates named: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation, product momentum, GW build-outs and execution, policy. Views on the primary overhang varied widely.

The desk says it is hard to separate the positive bottoms-up signals from the AI ecosystem from the top-down overhangs (rates, policy, price action, law of large numbers) that the Semis multiple compression may reflect.

Technicals point to possible counter-rallies in the coming days. Investors have lost conviction on what the durable clearing event is, which the desk says may suppress near-term re-grossing into the same names.
This week's earnings are a test: AI/Semi leaders (TTMI, LRCX, WDC) report alongside out-of-favor names (CMCSA, IBM, AT&T, INFY).

Top client inbounds: flows, feedback and credit; a late-week roll in AI Software names; earnings set-ups (META, SPCX, TXN, NFLX); defensive ideas (NFLX, SPOT, LYV, CSCO); what investors come back to first; whether earnings will matter; positioning in Memory (shorted or longed).
Low vol and Quality are working while Cyclicals lag. This hurt consensus positioning, and the GS HF VIP L/S pair (GSTHVIPP) had one of its bigger weekly drawdowns in recent memory.

Streaks: SOX on an 8-day losing streak (longest since 2008). R2K down 6 weeks in a row (longest since 2018). BKX down 6 straight weeks (longest since 2008). Consumer Discretionary lower in 9 of 10 weeks. Mag 7 outperformed NDX on 10 of 11 sessions. S&P 500 low-vol index up 7 days in a row. DIS completed a 10-day winning streak (longest since 2013).

Most oversold by 14-day RSI: INDI, CBRS, SITM, AMKR, WDC, STX, SKHY, SNDK, PLXS, FLEX, UCTT, ICHR, MKSI, AMAT, VRT, Neoclouds, SPHR. Most overbought: ERIC, VEEV, Dassault, PAYC, PCTY, BOX, Tata, CAN, MA, V, ADP, MKTX, CTAS, WMG, EBAY, CCI.

NDX forward P/E is 20.5x, the lowest since the AI cycle began in 2023, and only about a 1.8x premium to the S&P 500, the narrowest in nearly 10 years. Semis have de-rated from about 29x this summer to 17x forward P/E.
The SOX vs SPX relative drawdown is about 25% from the highs. The desk notes 20+ years of history suggest it may be getting close to a trough, phrased as a question.

AAPL is at all-time highs and just shy of retaking NVDA as the world's largest company. The desk calls it the clearest beneficiary of a flight-to-safety bid within tech, with a forward FCF yield of about 3.15%, above the NDX. Its 2-month rolling correlation to the NDX is inversely correlated for the first time in history.
SPXXAI (S&P 500 ex-AI) is closing the gap vs SPX as the correlation of AI and SPXXAI reverts lower.
Tighter financial conditions have historically coincided with rotation into defensives over cyclicals, per the desk's Financial Conditions Index chart.
Event calendar: NVDA GTC Berlin (Jensen Huang keynote Wed 10/21 at 5am ET), Cloudflare Connect, Zoomtopia, Money 20/20, Infineon OktoberTech Summit, AGNTCon + MCPCon Agent Summit.

tension_points.bear_case: Investors have lost conviction on what the durable clearing event is, which may suppress re-grossing into the same names. Top-down overhangs (rates, oil, policy, law of large numbers) and a debate on the linearity of the AI build-out persist, with AI capex about half of S&P 500 EPS growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: This week's AI/Semi earnings (TTMI, LRCX, WDC) are named as the telling test of whether the bull case holds.
